craft_notes: Sthāyin: outer-only (the demotion: oblation/sacrifice asked, answered as outer-procedure-in-gross-things). Rows: row 3 (what-how→outer). Close: deer-eyed (tenderness at the demotion — the address softens the refusal). Rejected: 'ritual is useless' — killed: outer kept (bāhya as location, not verdict; the inner was already answered); 'material offerings' — killed: gross things kept (sthūla as the text's own class-word).

lines: Whose oblation, whose sacrifice — what, and how?
outer procedure this, in gross things, deer-eyed.
l4.sanskrit_cite: hūyate kasya vā homo yāgaḥ kasya ca kiṃ katham | eṣātra prakriyā bāhyā sthūleṣv eva mṛgekṣaṇe

c1_essence: Outer oblations: procedures in gross things only.
